author: Mark Atwood
text: DESIGN CLARIFICATION 2026-05-12 (Mark, interactive): out-of-process integration (subprocess, IPC, daemon, network protocol) is acceptable for policy-adapter crates. FFI / in-process embedding (cgo for zlint, PyO3 for pkilint) is NOT required and not preferred -- adapter authors pick based on operational convenience. SUB-QUESTION RESOLVED: '.1 Subprocess vs FFI' for pkix-policy-zlint. Default to subprocess unless a specific reason for in-process surfaces. Likewise '.2 subprocess vs PyO3 vs HTTP wrapper' for pkix-policy-pkilint — subprocess is the default. ARCHITECTURAL JUSTIFICATION (consistent with prelaunch 'done right from the start' framing in AGENTS.md): subprocess preserves the workspace's small-Rust core, gives the maintainer zero burden on upstream-tool internals (zlint's Go modules, pkilint's Python deps), trivializes upgrades (binary swap, no rebuild), and has the smaller attack surface (no in-process Go runtime or CPython embedded). Perf cost (fork+exec per cert) is mitigated at the adapter API level via batch interfaces (one process per session, many certs) — design decision deferred to per-crate implementation. CROSS-CUTTING NOTE: PKIX-hbzo.1 (zlint + pkilint as cross-validation oracles in pkix-difftest) is currently scoped to subprocess oracles. With the runtime adapters also subprocess, there's significant code-sharing opportunity: subprocess plumbing, JSON parsing, finding normalization can be shared between the diff-test oracle and the runtime adapter. Worth deciding before either lands whether they share a crate (pkix-zlint-bridge?) or each implements its own. REMAINING OPEN SHAPE DECISIONS under this epic: (a) lint granularity — one workspace Lint per zlint check (700+ Lint instances) vs umbrella Lint per profile family (cabf-br-tls etc.); (b) zlint verdict (NA / NE / pass / notice / warn / error / fatal) -> workspace severity mapping; (c) batch interface shape — does the adapter expose 'lint these 1000 certs' as a single call, or N calls? (d) error handling when upstream binary missing / version mismatch; (e) whether to file pkix-policy-oscal as a real child or skip it. None of these have been made; surface to Mark when ready to decompose into implementation children.
